asof: Settles Thu 5 Nov 2026 · written Fri 6 Nov
headline: AI-stock rout pulls H7–U7 down 14–16.5bp; Z6/M7 hits target at +19.5bp, U7 peak at 4.335% is about a hike and a half.
summary: The strip bull-flattened hard on Thursday as a tech-stock rout drove haven buying: M7 and U7 fell 16.5bp to 4.305% and 4.335%, Z7 14.5bp to 4.325% and H7 14bp to 4.215%, while Z6 eased only 5bp to 4.11% and U6 0.7bp to 3.918%. Month-to-date the strip is now 3.5bp lower in Z6, 17.5–18.5bp lower in M7 and U7 and 11–12bp lower in the greens. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.335%, only 39.5bp over the 3.94% SOFR fixing, with 5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is a December hike plus about half of another, down from roughly two hikes on Wednesday and much closer to the consensus call of a December hike and a slower path after it.
drivers: AI-stock selloff sends money into the front end

The Nasdaq fell about 5% and the Philadelphia chip index about 9% on fears the new Democratic Congress will slow data-centre building, and Treasury yields fell by up to 9bp to the lowest since early September. Bloomberg said 2027 hike bets were pared and some STIR options targeted no December move. In SR3 the 2027 contracts led: H7 to Z7 fell 14–16.5bp in rate.
Oil keeps most of its slump

Brent settled at $94.62 on Wednesday after an 8.7% drop, its lowest since 31 August, and rebounded only about $2–3 on Thursday as Eurasia Group cut its odds of an Iran deal to 10%. Brent is still nearly a fifth below last Friday's peak near $118, which keeps pulling 2027 inflation risk lower even as the reds stayed bid.
Strong labour data and hawkish speakers anchor December

Jobless claims fell to 189,000 against about 196,000–197,000 expected, and the four-week average is the lowest since 1969; Q3 productivity rose 3.6% and unit labour costs fell 0.7%, both better than forecast. Hammack, who dissented for a hike in October, said policy must turn restrictive through smaller, more frequent moves, and Barkin also backed gradual hikes. Z6 fell only 5bp, so December stayed priced and the rally came from 2027.

SOFR fixed at 3.94% on 4 November, down 3bp, still 4bp above the 3.90% interest on reserves, 6bp over the 3.88% EFFR and 6bp under the 4.00% standing repo rate. U6 at 3.918% implied sits 2.2bp under the fixing.
spreads: The whites and reds bull-flattened sharply and the strip is now almost flat from the peak out. U6/Z6 narrowed 4.3bp to +19.2bp (−3.05bp on the month), Z6/H7 9bp to +10.5bp (−10.5bp), H7/M7 2.5bp to +9bp (−3.5bp) and M7/U7 held at +3bp, while U7/Z7 rose 2bp to −1bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 tightened 9.5bp to +21.5bp (−13.5bp month-to-date) and Z6/M7 11.5bp to +19.5bp (−14bp). Past the peak the inversion shrank: Z7/Z8 rose 6.5bp to −2.5bp (+5bp on the month), U7/Z8 8.5bp to −3.5bp and Z8/Z9 1.5bp to −1.5bp, with the green consecutive spreads between −1bp and 0. The H7/M7/U7 fly fell 2.5bp to +6bp and M7/U7/Z7 2bp to +4bp (both −2.5bp on the month). Week- and month-to-date changes are the same, as both run from the 30 October settle.
fed: The latest fed funds futures snapshot is Wednesday's, before Thursday's rally: 20.4bp for the 9 December meeting (an 82% chance of a hike), 25.5bp by January, 39.9bp by March, 52.4bp by June and a 54bp peak by July 2027 (implied EFFR 4.42%). That is up from 19.7bp for December a day earlier but 1–4bp lower further out (61bp peak), close to the 30 October month-end (17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp, 57bp peak) and far below 21.8bp, 31.5bp, 48.1bp, 67bp and a 75.5bp peak on 28 October. SR3 has since run well ahead of ZQ: the 4.42% peak plus SOFR's 6bp premium over EFFR is about 4.48%, 14.5bp above U7 at 4.335%, and Z6 at 4.11% sits about 8.5bp under the January ZQ level plus that premium. FedWatch still showed better than 80% for December on Thursday. With the peak now about a hike and a half away, SR3 is close to the Fed's September projections of one more move this year; Hammack and Barkin back gradual hikes, so payrolls on Friday (59,000–65,000 expected) and CPI on 10 November test whether Thursday's 2027 rally holds.

ideas.title: Sell the H7/M7 calendar spread (roll the 2027 fade)
ideas.why: The previous core, Z6/M7, hit its +20bp target as it settled at +19.5bp, 18.5bp in favour from the +38bp entry, so it is closed. The view is rolled into H7/M7 at +9bp, which still prices about a third of a hike between the March and June 2027 periods; with 6bp to target and 4bp to the stop, reward is 1.5 times risk. Oil nearly a fifth off last week's peak, falling unit labour costs and an AI-capex shock all argue against a steady run of 2027 hikes.
ideas.risk: After a 16.5bp one-day rally in M7, a firm payrolls print or hot CPI could snap 2027 hikes back and push the spread through +13bp.

ideas.title: Keep 2028 easing as the hedge: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open but 5.5bp against at −2.5bp, as Z7 fell 14.5bp in rate against 8bp for Z8 and the inversion past the peak shrank. It now hedges the core: if payrolls or CPI revive 2027 hikes, the reds sell off more than the greens and the spread falls. The target is cut to −12bp, just past Wednesday's −9bp, giving 9.5bp of reward against 3.5bp to the unchanged +1bp stop.
ideas.risk: A further risk-off rally that pulls Z7 toward Z8 would push the spread above +1bp and stop the hedge out.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through payrolls and refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 fell just 0.7bp to 3.918% implied on Thursday's rally, 2.2bp under the 3.94% SOFR fixing, which is still 4bp above the 3.90% interest on reserves and 6bp under the 4.00% standing repo rate. About $28bn of new refunding cash settles on 16 November and only U6's final week sees the December decision, so revisit after that settlement.
ideas.risk: If funding pressure fades, SOFR could slip back to 3.88–3.90% and leave a few bp on the table.

watch: 59,000–65,000 expected after 29,000, unemployment 4.2%, wages +0.3%; the first test of Thursday's 2027 rally and of the H7/M7 fade.
A deeper AI-stock selloff would extend the haven bid in the reds; an oil rebound on a breakdown in Iran talks would reverse it.
$58bn, the first refunding sale, tests front-end demand at two-month-low yields.
The last CPI before the December meeting after 3.7% headline in September; it sets Z6 and the December odds.
$25bn after the Veterans Day bond-market holiday on Wednesday; term premium and the greens.
Pipeline price pressure after the fall in unit labour costs; a firm print would support 2027 hikes.
About $28bn of new cash settles; a funding test for SOFR and U6.
